newsitem.title: USA: AT&T enters Chicago wireless service market.
newsitem.headline: AT&T enters Chicago wireless service market.

text.p: AT&T Wireless Services said Tuesday it entered Chicago's wireless phone market by launching its AT&T Digital PCS (personal communication systems) service.
PCS includes voice, paging and e-mail messaging capabilities.

Chicago is AT&T's third digital PCS market, following Phoenix and Atlanta as part of the company's nationwide roll-out of markets that were acquired for $1.7 billion in the 1995 Federal Communications Commission (FCC) spectrum auction.
AT&T said it expects to launch 10 new markets by the end of the year. AT&T provides wireless communications in the United States to more than 7 million customers.

AT&T said its digital PCS features dual-band (1900 MHz and 800 MHz) service. The phone can travel automatically between digital wireless systems and conventional analog systems, so customers can place and receive calls across the United States, Canada and Mexico where cellular service is available.
AT&T said it is offering a variety of calling plans, ranging from $24.99 a month with 45 included air-time minutes, to $99.00 per month for 400 included air-time minutes.
